rows.title: Cell Tracking Instance 1
rows.summary: Segment and track cells across a 30-frame fluorescence microscopy sequence and export Cell Tracking Challenge style masks and lineage metadata.
rows.task_prompt:
You are performing cell tracking on a fluorescence microscopy time-lapse sequence.

Task directory:
- `base`

Visible inputs:
- 30 grayscale TIFF frames: `base/input/01/t000.tif` through `base/input/01/t029.tif`
- Optional Python dependency manifest: `base/input/runtime_env/pyproject.toml`
- Optional Python dependency lockfile: `base/input/runtime_env/uv.lock`
- Optional Python wrapper: `base/software/python_cell_tracking.sh`

Recommended setup:
- Work on Linux in `base`.
- If you need common image-processing packages, run:
  `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/agenthle_cell_tracking_runtime_env uv sync --project "base/input/runtime_env"`
- You may run scripts through `base/software/python_cell_tracking.sh`.

Your task:
1. Segment individual cells in every frame.
2. Track cells across all 30 frames so the same cell keeps a consistent positive integer label.
3. Save labeled tracking masks as `base/output/mask000.tif` through `base/output/mask029.tif`.
4. Save the lineage table as `base/output/res_track.txt`.

Output format:
- Masks must be 2D labeled TIFF images with the same dimensions as the input frames.
- Pixel value `0` is background; positive integer values are cell IDs.
- `res_track.txt` must use Cell Tracking Challenge format with four whitespace-separated integer columns per row: `L B E P`.
- `L` is the cell label, `B` is the first frame index, `E` is the last frame index, and `P` is the parent label or `0`.

A successful result should accurately segment the cells and keep their identities consistent over time. Do not modify files under `input/`; write final result files only under `base/output`.
agent_must_do: Inspect the 30 staged fluorescence microscopy frames.
Segment individual cells in each frame.
Track cells over time with consistent positive integer labels.
Write exactly 30 labeled TIFF masks named `mask000.tif` through `mask029.tif`.
Write a valid CTC-style `res_track.txt` lineage table.

input_files.name: t000.tif ... t029.tif
input_files.description: Thirty grayscale 1024 by 1024 fluorescence microscopy frames.

input_files.name: pyproject.toml
input_files.description: Optional agent-runtime dependency manifest for common image-processing libraries.

input_files.name: uv.lock
input_files.description: Optional lockfile for reproducible agent-runtime dependency installation.

rows.title: Cell Translocation Analysis
rows.summary: Analyze paired DNA and GFP microscopy images to quantify nuclear translocation across a drug dose series and report the minimum effective dose.
rows.task_prompt:
You are analyzing two-channel cell microscopy images for GFP nuclear translocation.

Task directory:
- `base`

Visible inputs:
- Paired TIFF images: `base/input/images`
- Dose and control metadata: `base/input/images/Translocation_doses_and_controls.csv`
- Detailed task instructions: `base/input/task_instructions.md`
- Optional Python dependency manifest: `base/input/runtime_env/pyproject.toml`
- Optional Python wrapper: `base/software/python_cell_translocation.sh`

Your task is to pair the DNA and GFP channels by well, segment nuclei and cell/cytoplasm compartments, measure GFP and channel-correlation features, classify positive translocation using the dose/control metadata, identify the minimum effective dose, and save `Cells.csv`, `Cytoplasm.csv`, `Nuclei.csv`, and `answer.json` under `base/output`.

`answer.json` must be a JSON object with numeric keys `minimum_dose` and `positive_percentage`.

Do not modify files under `input/`.

## Analysis Contract

- Use the per-cell nuclear-to-cytoplasmic mean GFP intensity ratio as the translocation score. The control-established canonical positive classification is `Math_IntensityRatio > 4.0`; apply it unchanged to every well and do not retune it against dose-well responses.
- For each non-control dose, compute the fraction of segmented cells above the threshold. `minimum_dose` is the smallest non-control dose with a positive fraction of at least `0.80`; `positive_percentage` is that fraction at `minimum_dose`, on the `[0, 1]` scale and rounded to four decimal places.
- Write one row per segmented object in each measurement CSV. Every table must contain numeric `ImageNumber` and `ObjectNumber` columns, with `ImageNumber` consistently identifying the paired well image.
- `Cells.csv` must contain `Location_` features. `Cytoplasm.csv` and `Nuclei.csv` must contain `Correlation_`, `Intensity_`, `Location_`, and `Math_` feature families, including the translocation ratio as a `Math_` feature.
agent_must_do: Pair DNA (`w1`) and GFP (`w2`) TIFF images by well.
Segment nuclei and derive cell/cytoplasm compartments.
Measure GFP intensity, channel-correlation, location, and ratio-style object features.
Classify positive translocation using the dose/control metadata.
Save `Cells.csv`, `Cytoplasm.csv`, `Nuclei.csv`, and `answer.json` under the runtime output directory.

input_files.name: BBBC013_<well>_s1_w1.tif / BBBC013_<well>_s1_w2.tif
input_files.description: Paired DNA and GFP microscopy channels for each staged well.

input_files.name: Translocation_doses_and_controls.csv
input_files.description: Well-to-dose and control metadata.

input_files.name: runtime_env
input_files.description: Optional pinned Python image-analysis runtime.

rows.title: Single-FOV MERFISH Image Decoding And Cell Segmentation
rows.summary: Run the full MERFISH image-analysis pipeline on one field of view of U2OS cells: decode transcripts against a 130-gene MHD4 codebook, segment nuclei from the DAPI tile, assign transcripts to cells, and emit a cell-by-gene count matrix plus quality metrics.
rows.task_prompt:
You are working on an Ubuntu VM to run the full MERFISH image-analysis pipeline
for one field of view of a human U2OS cell population stained against a
130-gene panel.

Task directory:
- `base`

Inputs (all under `base/input`; treat as read-only):
- `experiment.json` plus `primary_images.json`, `nuclei.json` and the per-FOV
  manifests `primary_images-fov_000.json` / `nuclei-fov_000.json`. These
  describe a starfish Experiment with one FOV, 8 hybridization rounds, and
  2 color channels.
- 16 primary fluorescence TIFFs
  `primary_images-fov_000-Z0-H<h>-C<c>.tiff` (h in 0..7, c in 0..1); each is
  2048x2048.
- 1 DAPI nuclear stain TIFF `nuclei-fov_000-Z0-H0-C0.tiff`.
- `codebook.json` mapping 130 target genes and 10 Blank controls to 16-bit
  MHD4 (Hamming-distance-4 with 1-bit error correction) binary codewords.
- `experiment.json` `extras.scale_factors` gives per-(round, channel)
  normalization scalars.
- `output_contract.json` lists the exact output files, columns, and dtypes
  your pipeline must produce.
- `runtime_env/pyproject.toml`, `runtime_env/uv.lock`, and
  `runtime_env/python-version` pin the Python 3.11 environment that
  starfish 0.3.4 and Cellpose 3.1.1 need. The canonical agent-facing entry
  point `base/software/merfish_runtime.sh`
  behaves like a Python interpreter, keeps its `uv` cache and resolved
  environment under `base/output`,
  and uses `runtime_env/pyproject.toml` (with the staged `uv.lock`) as the
  frozen runtime manifest. You can invoke it directly
  (`software/merfish_runtime.sh your_script.py`) or materialize the env
  yourself with `uv sync --frozen --project input/runtime_env` and then run
  the resulting `.venv/bin/python`.

Recommended workflow:
1. Load the starfish Experiment and sanity-check the image and codebook.
2. Preprocess: high-pass filter or background-subtract, normalize intensity
   using the provided `scale_factors`, and confirm the pre-registered tiles
   are still aligned.
3. Run starfish BlobDetector on each round/channel and extract 16-bit
   intensity traces per spot.
4. Decode with an MHD4-aware decoder (starfish `CheckAll`) with 1-bit error
   correction; filter by magnitude and distance thresholds.
5. Run Cellpose on the DAPI image with a pretrained nuclei model and a
   diameter appropriate for U2OS (roughly 30-50 px).
6. Assign decoded transcripts to the nearest segmented cell; mark transcripts
   outside every cell as extracellular and exclude them from the
   cell-by-gene matrix.
7. Build the cell-by-gene count matrix for the 130 real genes (exclude
   blanks) and compute the quality metrics listed in `output_contract.json`.

Outputs must go into `base/output`:
- `decoded_transcripts.csv` with columns `gene, x, y, is_exact, total_magnitude`.
- `segmentation.tiff` - 2048x2048 `uint16` labeled mask (background=0).
- `cell_by_gene.csv` - leading `cell_id` column followed by the 130 real genes
  in codebook order; integer counts.
- `quality_metrics.json` - scalar keys `total_decoded_transcripts`,
  `blank_rate`, `exact_match_fraction`, `n_cells`, `assigned_fraction`,
  `mean_transcripts_per_cell`.

All coordinates (`x`, `y`) in `decoded_transcripts.csv` must be pixel
coordinates within the 2048x2048 FOV so they line up with the segmentation
mask.
agent_must_do: Invoke the canonical Python entry point `software/merfish_runtime.sh` (or materialize the env with `uv sync --frozen --project input/runtime_env/`).
Load the staged starfish experiment (16 primary TIFFs + 1 DAPI TIFF + manifests + codebook) and sanity-check alignment.
Preprocess images: high-pass / background subtract, apply per-(round, channel) `scale_factors`, confirm registration.
Detect fluorescent spots with starfish `BlobDetector` and decode with the MHD4-aware `CheckAll` decoder plus 1-bit error correction.
Segment nuclei from the DAPI tile using Cellpose 3.1.1 with the `nuclei` model and a diameter around 30-50 px for U2OS cells.
Assign decoded transcripts to the nearest labeled cell and mark out-of-cell transcripts as extracellular.
Emit `decoded_transcripts.csv`, `segmentation.tiff`, `cell_by_gene.csv`, and `quality_metrics.json` under `output/` in pixel coordinates.

rows.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Spatial Domain Identification
rows.summary: Cluster 12 human DLPFC 10x Visium slices into spatial domains and submit per-spot labels, summary metrics, manifest metadata, and one UMAP overlay.
rows.task_prompt:
You are given 12 human DLPFC 10x Visium slices and must identify spatial domains on every slice.

Task directory:
- `base`

Visible inputs:
- Slice data directories: `base/input/data/<slice_id>/`
- Per-slice target cluster counts: `base/input/data/slice_config.csv`
- Optional Python runtime manifest: `base/input/runtime_env/pyproject.toml`
- Optional Python lockfile: `base/input/runtime_env/uv.lock`
- Baseline uv wrapper: `base/software/uv`
- Baseline Python 3.12 wrapper: `base/software/python3.12`
- Detailed task prompt: `base/input/task_prompt.md`

If you need the staged spatial transcriptomics stack, run `base/software/uv sync --frozen --python 3.12 --project base/input/runtime_env`.

Required outputs under `base/output`:
- `summary.csv` with header `slice_id,n_spots_scored,n_clusters_pred,ari,nmi`
- `manifest.json` with method metadata, an integer seed, and graph/embedding/clustering flags
- `per_slice/<slice_id>_labels.csv` for all 12 slices with header `barcode,predicted_label`
- `umap_overlay_151673.png`

Use the exact per-slice target cluster counts from `slice_config.csv`, treat `input/` as read-only, and keep solver-created files under `output/`.
agent_must_do: Load the staged matrix, features, barcodes, and spatial-coordinate files for all 12 Visium slices.
Use `input/data/slice_config.csv` as the exact target number of clusters per slice.
Run an unsupervised spatial-domain identification workflow.
Write one `per_slice/<slice_id>_labels.csv` file per slice with `barcode,predicted_label` columns.
Write `summary.csv`, `manifest.json`, and `umap_overlay_151673.png` under the runtime output directory.

input_files.description: Per-slice Visium count matrices and feature/barcode tables.

input_files.description: Per-slice tissue positions and scale factors.

input_files.description: Per-slice subject IDs and required cluster counts.

input_files.description: Task-local wrappers for the VM baseline uv and Python 3.12 tools.

rows.title: Marrow Cell Type Annotation
rows.summary: Annotate every cell in a staged Smart-seq2 mouse bone marrow AnnData object using a fixed 21-label ontology and return one predicted label per cell.
rows.task_prompt:
You are given an unlabeled Smart-seq2 mouse bone marrow single-cell dataset and must annotate every cell with one label from a fixed 21-class ontology.

Task directory:
- `base`

Visible inputs:
- AnnData matrix: `base/input/tms_marrow_unlabeled.h5ad`
- Allowed labels: `base/input/allowed_labels.txt`
- Agent-facing runtime manifest: `base/input/runtime_env/pyproject.toml`
- Agent-facing runtime lockfile: `base/input/runtime_env/uv.lock`
- Task note: `base/input/input.txt`

Recommended setup:
- Work on Linux in `base`
- If you need Scanpy / AnnData tooling, install from the staged runtime with:
  `uv sync --frozen --project "base/input/runtime_env"`

Required output:
- Write exactly one UTF-8 CSV to `base/output/predictions.csv`
- Keep the header exactly `cell_id,predicted_cell_type`
- Emit exactly one row for every input cell
- Use only labels from `base/input/allowed_labels.txt`

Relevant metadata available in the AnnData object includes:
- `age`
- `mouse.id`
- `sex`
- `n_genes`
- `n_counts`

Do not ask for confirmation. Execute directly.
agent_must_do: Load the staged Smart-seq2 marrow AnnData object on Linux and, if needed, install the staged Python runtime from `input/runtime_env/` with `uv`.
Run a biologically reasonable batch-aware single-cell annotation workflow across the fixed 21-label ontology.
Write exactly one UTF-8 CSV to `output/predictions.csv` with header `cell_id,predicted_cell_type` and one row per input cell.

input_files.name: tms_marrow_unlabeled.h5ad
input_files.description: Unlabeled Smart-seq2 mouse bone marrow AnnData object with 14,517 cells.

input_files.name: allowed_labels.txt
input_files.description: Exact 21-label ontology allowed for `predicted_cell_type`.

input_files.description: Short task note summarizing the runtime contract.

input_files.description: Agent-facing Python runtime manifest for Scanpy / AnnData tooling.

input_files.description: Locked dependency resolution for the staged runtime.

rows.title: Yeast Colony Detection
rows.summary: Detect red yeast colonies in a masked agar-plate image and export a colony count plus centroid measurement table.
rows.task_prompt:
You are analyzing a yeast colony plate image on Linux.

## Your Task
Detect the red yeast colonies growing on the agar plate while excluding white dots and other visual noise.

## Visible Inputs
- Plate image: `base/input/6-1.jpg`
- Plate-region mask: `base/input/PlateTemplate.png`
- CellProfiler entry point, if provisioned: `base/software/cellprofiler`

## What You Must Do
1. Use the plate image and mask to identify red yeast colonies inside the plate region.
2. Create a reproducible detection workflow in CellProfiler 4.2.8 or another image-analysis workflow available on the VM.
3. Count the detected red colonies.
4. Save all required outputs under `base/output`.

## Required Outputs
- JSON count file: `base/output/answer.json`
  - exact schema: `{"colony_count": <integer>}`
- Measurement CSV: `base/output/measurements/RedColonies.csv`
  - include one row per detected red colony
  - include numeric centroid columns named `Location_Center_X` and `Location_Center_Y`
  - include `ObjectNumber` if your workflow can provide it

## Constraints
- Do not modify files under `base/input`.
- Only read the visible files under `base/input`.
- Keep all task-produced files inside `base/output`.
agent_must_do: Use the plate image and mask to identify red yeast colonies inside the plate region.
Exclude white dots and unrelated visual noise from the colony detections.
Create a reproducible CellProfiler or image-analysis workflow on the Linux VM.
Write `answer.json` with an integer `colony_count`.
Write `measurements/RedColonies.csv` with one row per detected colony and numeric centroid columns.

input_files.name: 6-1.jpg
input_files.description: Yeast agar plate image.

input_files.name: PlateTemplate.png
input_files.description: Aligned plate-region mask.
